content.summary: In this reading module, you will explore texts about music concerts, different music genres, and how people book tickets online and at ticket counters. You will learn useful phrases to ask about ticket prices, seat locations, and payment options politely.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Using polite modal verbs like would like and could, plus question structures for availability and prices.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to live music events, concert venues, ticket booking, and musical instruments.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning short announcements and dialogues to quickly find specific details such as dates, times, and seat numbers.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about concerts and music events.
Locate specific details such as ticket prices, dates, and seat rows in dialogues and schedules.
Recognize and practice polite structures for booking tickets and expressing music preferences.

contextWarmup.prompt: You want to buy a ticket for a rock concert this weekend. Where do you usually look for available seats?
options: On the official venue website or ticket app
contextWarmup.explanation: Official venue websites and ticket apps are the best places to check schedules, seat availability, and book tickets for live concerts.

rules: Asking about availability: Use 'Are there any seats available for [day/time]?' or 'Do you have tickets for [event]?' to check ticket options.
Inquiring about price: Use 'How much is the ticket?' or 'What is the price for VIP seats?' to ask about costs.
Discussing payment: Use 'Can I pay by credit card?' or 'Do you accept cash?' when paying for your booking.
Expressing preferences: Use 'I prefer acoustic music' or 'I would like seats near the stage' to state your choices politely.
Confirming booking: Use 'I would like to book two tickets for Friday night' to complete your reservation.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Confusing Would Like with Present Simple Want
commonTrap.explanation: Learners sometimes use 'I want' in polite ticket booking situations. In customer service and polite requests, 'I would like' is much more natural and polite.
commonTrap.wrong: I want two tickets for the rock concert.
commonTrap.correct: I would like two tickets for the rock concert, please.

contractions.exampleContracted: I'd like to book two tickets.

contractions.exampleFull: We will meet at the concert venue.
contractions.exampleContracted: We'll meet at the concert venue.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns for Booking Tickets
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice polite requests and statements:

items.exampleSentence: The concert venue is located in the city center.
The band will perform on the main stage tonight.
The audience gave a standing ovation after the performance.
She loves acoustic guitar music more than electric.
The electric guitar solo was amazing.
Are there any seats available for Saturday evening?
I need to confirm my booking before the concert.
What genre of music do you prefer - rock or jazz?
We have seats in row 5, close to the stage.
What payment methods do you accept for tickets?

paragraphs: Last Friday, Sarah and her friend Leo decided to go to a live music concert this weekend. They checked a popular ticketing website to see what music genres were available in their city. Leo loves electric rock music, but Sarah prefers acoustic guitar melodies and gentle singing.

After looking at several options, they found an amazing concert at the City Hall venue. The headline band plays both acoustic and electric songs. Sarah read the seating chart carefully and chose two seats in row five, right near the main stage. They entered their credit card information for the payment and received a digital booking confirmation on their phones.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Booking Tickets on the Phone

content.context: Sarah is calling the City Arena box office to book tickets for a jazz concert this weekend.
content.audioPrompt: Listen to the phone conversation between Sarah and the box office clerk.

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: City Arena box office. How can I help?
lines.translation: Box office City Arena. Ada yang bisa saya bantu?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Hi, I need tickets for Friday night.
lines.translation: Hai, saya butuh tiket untuk malam Jumat.

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: Are you interested in the jazz concert?
lines.translation: Apakah Anda tertarik dengan konser jazz?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes, exactly. Are there any seats left?
lines.translation: Ya, tepat sekali. Apakah masih ada kursi tersisa?

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: We have balcony seats for thirty dollars.
lines.translation: Kami punya kursi balkon seharga tiga puluh dolar.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That sounds great. I want two tickets.
lines.translation: Terdengar bagus. Saya mau dua tiket.

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: That is sixty dollars in total.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Can I pay by credit card?
lines.translation: Bisakah saya membayar dengan kartu kredit?

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: Yes, we accept all major cards.
lines.translation: Ya, kami menerima semua kartu utama.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Great. What time does the show start?

lines.speaker: Box Office Clerk
lines.text: Doors open at seven thirty tonight.
lines.translation: Pintu dibuka jam tujuh tiga puluh malam ini.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Thank you so much for your help.
lines.translation: Terima kasih banyak atas bantuan Anda.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Music Concert Tickets and Preferences

content.summary: Practical guide on sentence structure to ask about ticket availability, inquire about prices, and express music preferences in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Asking About Ticket Availability
blueprintItems.example: Are there any tickets available for the rock concert on Saturday?

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Inquiring About Price and Seat Types
blueprintItems.formula: How much are the [seat type] tickets for [event]?
blueprintItems.example: How much are the front row tickets for the jazz festival?

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Expressing Preferences and Booking
blueprintItems.formula: I prefer [genre/seat] and I would like to book [number] tickets.
blueprintItems.example: I prefer pop music and I would like to book two tickets for Friday night.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize music genres when they start a sentence, but keep them lowercase in the middle of a sentence unless they are proper names.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i love listening to Rock and pop music.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I love listening to rock and pop music.
mechanicsRules.why: Music genres are common nouns in English and do not need capitalization in the middle of sentences.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always use question marks at the end of availability and price inquiries.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Are there any seats left for the concert.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Are there any seats left for the concert?
mechanicsRules.why: Direct questions require a question mark punctuation mark at the end.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use capital letters for proper names of concert venues, bands, and days of the week.
mechanicsRules.badExample: we are seeing coldplay at wembley stadium on friday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: We are seeing Coldplay at Wembley Stadium on Friday.
mechanicsRules.why: Band names, venue names, and days are proper nouns and require initial capital letters.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a negative sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: She wants to buy tickets for the rock concert.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use doesn't want instead of wants.
targetAnswers: She doesn't want to buy tickets for the rock concert.
She does not want to buy tickets for the rock concert.
practicumQuestions.explanation: For third-person singular in the present simple tense, use doesn't before the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the statement into a direct question asking about ticket availability:
practicumQuestions.promptText: There are seats available for the jazz show.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with Are there and end with a question mark.
targetAnswers: Are there seats available for the jazz show?
practicumQuestions.explanation: To form a yes or no question with there are, invert the words to Are there.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the conjunction because:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I want to buy front row seats. I love seeing the band up close.
practicumQuestions.hint: Place because between the two clauses to show the reason.
targetAnswers: I want to buy front row seats because I love seeing the band up close.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because connects the main action with the reason why you want those specific seats.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the conjunction and:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Liam likes pop music. Sarah prefers classical music.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use and to connect two independent clauses.
targetAnswers: Liam likes pop music, and Sarah prefers classical music.
Liam likes pop music and Sarah prefers classical music.
practicumQuestions.explanation: And links two parallel musical preferences in a compound sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix all capitalization and punctuation errors in the sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: are there any tickets left for friday
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first letter and the day of the week, and add a question mark.
targetAnswers: Are there any tickets left for Friday?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Sentences must start with a capital letter, days like Friday need a capital letter, and questions need a question mark.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the punctuation and capitalization in the following sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: i would like to pay by credit card for the concert
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the pronoun I and add a period at the end.
targetAnswers: I would like to pay by credit card for the concert.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The pronoun I must always be capitalized, and complete sentences require a period at the end.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a short sentence answering what your favorite music genre is:
practicumQuestions.promptText: What is your favorite music genre?
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with My favorite music genre is...
targetAnswers: My favorite music genre is rock.
My favorite music genre is pop.
My favorite music genre is jazz.
My favorite music genre is classical.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a complete subject-verb structure to state your musical preference clearly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a short question asking about the price of balcony tickets:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Ask about the price of balcony tickets.
targetAnswers: How much are the balcony tickets?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use How much are to inquire about plural ticket prices.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the affirmative sentence into a negative sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: He likes listening to heavy metal music.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use doesn't like or does not like.
targetAnswers: He doesn't like listening to heavy metal music.
He does not like listening to heavy metal music.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In the present simple tense, third-person singular negative sentences use doesn't plus the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capitalization and punctuation in this booking confirmation sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: we want to book two tickets for the concert on saturday
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word and the day of the week.
targetAnswers: We want to book two tickets for the concert on Saturday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper sentences start with a capital letter, days of the week require capitals, and sentences end with a period.

content.summary: This module helps you speak clearly about music genres, describe live concerts, and book tickets politely at a box office or online desk.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to sentence stress when talking about prices, row numbers, and musical instruments. Keep your voice polite and clear when asking for ticket details.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear pronunciation of vowels in music terms
pillars.explanation: Pronounce vowels distinctly in words like venue, stage, and genre to ensure listeners understand your musical preferences.

pillars.name: Polite Intonation
pillars.target: Rising and falling tones for requests
pillars.explanation: Use a polite rising tone when asking questions about available tickets and seat rows.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Both musical instrument adjectives place their primary stress on the second syllable.
Nouns related to concert settings and categories put the main stress on the first syllable.
Concert event terms emphasize the opening syllable for clear pronunciation.
Ticket purchasing terms maintain steady stress patterns on the primary content syllables.
